question: Fisher’s quantity theory is explained by his famous equation given as ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**MV = PT.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fisher's quantity theory:-**

 
 
• It​ is a monetary theory that explains the relationship between** money supply, velocity of money, price level, and output**.
 
• The famous equation given by Fisher is **MV = PT, **where M is the money supply, V is the velocity of money, P is the price level, and T is the level of transactions.
 
• The equation suggests that an** increase in the money supply **(M) will lead to an **increase** in the price level (P), assuming that the velocity of money (V) and the level of transactions (T) are** constant.**
 
• The theory also implies that changes in the** money supply** have a direct impact on inflation, as an increase in the money supply leads to an **increase in the price level**, which in turn reduces the purchasing power of money.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The quantity theory of money has been subject to** criticism** over the years, with some economists arguing that it **oversimplifies the complex dynamics** of the economy.
 
• One of the criticisms is that the **velocity of money** is **not constant **and can vary significantly over time, making it difficult to predict the** impact of changes in the money supply **on the price level.
 
• Another criticism is that the theory assumes that the** level of transactions is fixed**, which is not always the case as it can be influenced by a variety of factors such as technology, demographics, and government policies.
